items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: I understand Kid Horry's band did something like that in California.

ctx.x: the whole thing. Even the last chorus they wouldn't blare out on it.

Oh no, even the last chorus would be real quiet. It would fade away. And you could really hear the dancers' feet shuffling on the floor. Every now and then one of the musicians in the band would swell up, like the bass player would get louder, and then get sink down, or maybe the trombone would swell, and then it would come back. But it had a very strange, dreamy effect. It started to get to the point where you couldn't be sure whether you were actually hearing the clarinet play a phrase, or whether you imagined…
Yeah, they would do things almost like that. I heard them almost that way. Not much, because I never heard them at their very best, but I heard them pretty good.

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: later on, I think he went out and, and, uh, uh, did something similar with Kid Orrie's band, I believe.

ctx.x: Well, who seemed to be running the thing, just from the standpoint of an outsider?

Well, I guess Gene was running it. Uh, uh, he had some kind of, uh, tie-in with the owner of the Stuyvesant, Mr. Menschel or something like that. And, uh, as far as I know, it was Gene that, uh, that engineered the thing. And, uh, later on, I think he went out and, and, uh, uh, did something similar with Kid Orrie's band, I believe. I know he was quite active.
What kind of guy was Gene? What kind of fellow do you seem to be on a pair? Again, uh, just seeing him.
